caption:
🚣‍♀️💙 Meet the Engaged Athlete Fellows!
Today, we’re spotlighting Anika Roche, a student-athlete on the UCLA Rowing team.

For Anika, civic engagement has been a lifelong passion—and being an Engaged Athlete Fellow has given her the tools, resources, and community to turn that passion into action. Through the fellowship, she’s educating her peers about their civic duties, organizing events on campus, and leading efforts that strengthen civic participation at UCLA and beyond.

Anika’s year-long project focuses on expanding California’s 2019 Student Civic and Voter Empowerment Act (AB 963) to include the University of California campuses. By advocating for this expansion, she’s helping ensure that student-athletes and students across the UC system have meaningful access to civic engagement programming and the opportunity to make their voices heard. Rooted in education, advocacy, and leadership, Anika’s work demonstrates the power of athletes to drive lasting civic impact—far beyond the water. 🌊📚✨

caption:
Congratulations to our PACE (Pacific Islanders and Asians Committed to Excellence) track athlete, @kahocichon for her performance at her first indoor meet of the season! Here’s her message for everyone: 

My name is Kaho Cichon, and I’m a fourth-year on the UCLA Track & Field team. I competed in the 1K at Spokane in our first indoor meet of the season, and it felt exciting to be back on the track and racing again. This race gave me a lot of confidence heading into both the indoor and outdoor seasons.
Representing the AAPI community in track & field means a great deal to me, especially because we are often underrepresented in athletics as a whole. I hope to do my part by being the representation—and inspiration—I wish I had growing up. It was amazing to see so many of my teammates perform so well at our first meet, and it felt especially empowering to see several event winners who were also fellow AAPI athletes. I’m incredibly excited for what this season has in store.

caption:
Join us Saturday 2/28 for a FREE Football Camp 🏈

We’re excited to welcome Omar Staple (Oakland Tech High School) and Jaivian Thomas (McClymonds High School)—two athletes who trained with us during their high school off-seasons and continued preparing here for their college football careers. They’re coming back to share firsthand knowledge on how to make the most of your off-season and what it really takes to level up.

The camp will be facilitated by Coach Jason Romero, alongside our coaching staff.

We’ll be hosting two sessions:
• Ages 9–13
• Ages 14–18

Athletes will cover the fundamentals of speed, agility, and strength, while also touching on mobility and nutrition to support proper recovery. Come ready to learn and ready to work.

What to bring? Comfortable preferably flat shoes and a water bottle. No cleats. 

This camp is 100% free, but spots are limited and registration is required. Each session will be capped at 28 athletesso we can provide focused coaching and attention.

👉 Register via the link in our bio
Please feel free to share this with athletes and families who would benefit.

Get Bent Friends is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. If you’d like to donate or get involved as a volunteer, reach out to Coach Jason.

athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with a fierce determination, this ATK blends precise footwork with tactical intelligence. Hailing from a rich soccer heritage, he thrives under pressure, inspiring teammates with his unwavering spirit.

caption:
Where it started to where it ended 🤽‍♂️

Crazy to think that these five years went so fast. Seems like just yesterday I took my first steps onto Spieker Aquatics Center as an overly eager freshman ready to begin the grueling summer session. Reflecting back on polo through the years, I see now that it has given me some very important insights. College ball taught me that it is less about the winning and losing, but rather the identity that you create. A win or a loss never defines you. I have been on both sides; whether it was winning a national championship or losing a tournament by bobbling the ball on the last shot of a shootout. The constant work and dedication one puts into a sport defines who they are. I have seen talent come and go but in the end hard work is the only thing that prevails. College water polo is officially done, but I am one of the few that gets to continue. Looking at all of my past teammates who had to leave the sport helps me appreciate the position I am in. I have much more to learn and experience, and I can’t wait for what my journey holds. Happy Holidays and can’t wait for 2026 🥂🥂

caption:
This past year has gone far from expected, but man oh man the lessons learned! 

Thank you UCLA volleyball for giving me some of my best friends and closest relationships! I love this team and am grateful to wear these four letters on my chest. 

In reflection of this past season, I have learned that true confidence only comes from yourself and God. Trials may seem far from what you wish, but the Lord gives you what you NEED, not just what you want. My indoor collegiate career has been far from easy, and what I can say after 4.5 years, is that never give someone else or some thing the power to take away your love for the game. Amidst the hardships, I truly have become the most resilient and confident version of myself. 

My indoor career is far from over, and I can leave this chapter as a better person and player. First things first though, time to get sandy💜 @lsubeachvb

Long Jump Breakdown Pt 106 ft @allan__hunter 
.
Smooth and control>>>>
.
Some notes
.
Allan here pops off w a 7.90m and a lot of it has to do with him keeping his hip height, his speed, and foot beneath him so he can take as much of that speed with him through his jump. Now, at full speed it does look like he slowed up a bit coming into the jump, which to me means maybe he needed to module it down just a bit to manage all the forces. There’s a lot more in that jump, and it’s also a great example of what an approach looks like with limited leakages down the runway 
.
He could also be a little more timely in getting into that seated in air chair position, so he could swing down more fully and get into the pike position. I wonder if trailing his arms and legs behind him has something to do with it. I do the same landing so I know how for me it can give me little time to prep and swing into pike - where I often cheat and don’t complete a full sweep so my legs drop. If he did, maybe the next jump is 8m!!

caption:
It’s hard to put into words what this program means to me.
I committed to UCLA when I was 15, and never could I have imagined that my collegiate career would unfold the way it did. I wouldn’t change a single part of the past 3.5 years. I’ve grown as a player, but more importantly, as a person. 

To Marg, Molly, Gof, Molly, and the entire support staff: thank you. Thank you for taking a chance on me and believing in me. I can confidently say there is no better staff. No staff more knowledgeable, more caring, or more joyful. It’s a privilege to have been coached by you.

To my teammates: thank you for pushing me every single day. I am where I am because of each and every one of you. 

To this year’s team: you are all destined for greatness. I’ve never been part of a group that felt more like family than this one.

A mi familia: gracias por el amor constante, los sacrificios y el apoyo. Sin ustedes, nada de esto sería posible. 

It’s hard to imagine not wearing those four letters across my chest again, but I’m at peace knowing that UCLA, and God’s guidance through it all, have prepared me for everything ahead. 4s Up forever 💙🧸

caption:
Well 3 programs in 4 years has been a CRAZY ride but my last season was nothing short of an answered prayer and a blessing. God continuously provided and showed up in my life in every single way possible. Transferring to UCLA was one of the best decisions of my life. Gof, Marg, Molly, Molly and everyone on staff healed me in so many different ways. The girls I met along the way in such a short amount of time are people that I will forever have in my life. Thank you for the best senior season I could’ve ever imagined. I will forever be a bruin and cheer on UCLA wsoc 🐻💙

My time at TCU pushed me to limits I never thought I could reach as a person and a player. I wouldn’t be the player or person that I am today without experiencing 2 1/2 years there. From living with my best friends in a house with 7 people to having the best laughs and locker room dances I will always remember. Last but not least being baptized with all my favorite people around me. My life completely changed with being around so many God fearing women and eventually, leading me to Him and saving my life. Thank you TCU💜💜

Thank you LMU for taking a chance on me, thank you for giving me an opportunity. As a freshman there came so many ups and downs but it set me up for everything that was going to come in my future. Genuinely some of the funniest girls I’ve met and so happy to have experienced it. 

Thank you college soccer for being so difficult but rewarding. These past 4 years went by so fast but there was no other place or people I’d rather end it with ❤️

last sunday for @audreyallen17 and i:

5:00am CT - wake up
6:30am CT - walk a mile to @happycamperchicago while carrying all of our earthly belongings
7:20am CT - cover the chicago marathon, me on the @citiusmag live watchalong and audrey shooting photos and doing socials
10:30am CT - dodge hundreds of runners to cross the course and make our uber to midway 15 minutes after the watchalong ended
12:20pm CT - board flight back to orlando
5:30pm ET - start driving back to gainesville
7:58pm ET - make our anniversary dinner reservation at 8 just in time

honestly a pretty normal day by our standards because we have the coolest jobs in the world and are so lucky to go to so many awesome places together. first major marathon weekend for both of us and it was a roaring success mainly just because i got to see the willis tower.

talking thons with @_ericjenkins, @kare_les and @macfleet was as an absolute pleasure, especially while repping @throw_town_ramona for (at the time of publication) 133k distance fans to see. audrey clipped an ungodly amount of reels on saturday and crushed shooting on sunday (just go look at the citius feed) bc my gf is so cool.

TL;DR - nice time in chicago, let’s do it again sometime

athlete.bio: A fierce competitor with a relentless work ethic, this player combines agility and precision on the field. Off the pitch, her infectious enthusiasm and teamwork inspire camaraderie among teammates.

caption:
About a year ago I posted about missing running. A year later, I’m still out—not just from competition, but from practice too.
After months of doctor appointments and confusion, wondering why I was slowing down and why simple runs felt so dramatic and exhausting despite (trying) to train again, I finally got answers. I was diagnosed with POTS.
It explains why my body couldn’t recover and had to keep stopping on a mile run. It’s a relief to finally understand, but hard not knowing what this means for my running future. Delusion and motivation are keeping me going to come back with my teammates. 
•
As David Goggins once said… embrace the suck 😌💙 
#stayhydrated #gobruins

athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with a fierce determination, her graceful strides and tactical acumen set her apart. Raised in the mountains, she embodies resilience, thriving in challenges both on and off the track.

caption:
so you’re telling me that two of my bosses brought me to cover the world champs in tokyo, and my other boss let me borrow a camera to capture my time there? 🌎💻😛🏟️🇯🇵

i worked 17 track meets on the ground this season (that’s my #!), and was probably doing a completely different thing at each one. sometimes i was posted up at the finish line with my camera shooting photo or video, others i had my laptop open pumping the social channels from some of the best seats in the house. many times it was both!

thank you @chris_j_chavez @macfleet @citiusmag for breaking my 22-year streak of carrying around an empty passport and giving me a life-and-career-changing opportunity. shoutout @vhwone for the @fujifilmx_us (i want to keep learning how to use it) and sharing your excitement about our content because track and field and everyone involved is something special.

i’m proud of the many “events” i try my best to do on the media side of this sport, and i hope to keep getting better at each of them. i’m lucky i get to work with so many teams, and i’m excited to gain experience in other sports this coming year as well. and i’m grateful for how much i’ve gotten to travel in 2025, even though sometimes i may forget i’m still a student in the classroom…

that said, track and field/xc doesn’t sleep and neither do i, so see y’all at gans creek 😄🫡 i love my job.

oh and of course i can’t believe i get to do it all with @phofmahoney!

📸 @jzsnapz for slide 8

athlete.name: Audrey Allen
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with a fierce determination, her graceful strides and tactical acumen set her apart. Raised in the mountains, she embodies resilience, thriving in challenges both on and off the track.

caption:
i lost my best friend this summer. i went home this weekend to celebrate cassy’s life, and i gave a speech at her memorial that i also wanted to share here: 

after i found out, it took me a few weeks to write anything at all. then i didn’t pick it back up until the plane to california on friday. this didn’t make sense to me, i think i was in a state of denial and didn’t want to face it. cassy and i went from seeing each other for every part of our every days in high school to only once or twice a year when we were in college. this loss feels different because of the way our relationship was these last few years, i feel like she’s still just one text or phone call away. 

it happened when i was in eugene working at NCAAs. my mom called me with the news, i don’t even know how she went about doing that, but it was the worst, and the shortest, phone call i’ve ever received. i’ve never uncontrollably shaken from crying before. paul cried too, and he hadn’t even met cassy in person yet. she just had that impact on people. which is why i wanted also to type these words here, because she touched more people than were able to be there this weekend. 

some asked how i still worked, and i don’t really know how i did. cassy, and our sport, made me learn how to distract myself from pain. but the second the meet was over for the day and that distraction was gone i broke down again. i became a regular as the sobbing girl in the 10pm chipotle line. i couldn’t drive more than 30 minutes of the 9 hours it took to get back from oregon because i couldn’t think straight. coming home didn’t feel the same. 

even two months later, i probably only drove a quarter of the cross country trek to move to florida - not because i couldn’t think straight, but because i was scared. i wanted a sense of control but i still felt out of control. death is a very real thing. 

cassy and i would talk about how funny it was that we went from spending every day together to being across the world from each other, yet somehow we got closer these last few months. every penny of that $270 phone bill i was charged from AT&T for being too naive to use whatsapp was worth every penny. caption:
I’ve been training with pixie dust and happy thoughts this summer, as my Grandpa told me to, and now I’m starting to fly again🧚🏼 

Every athlete sidelined by injuries or health struggles knows how absolutely frustrating it is when your body won’t let you do what you want for yourself and your team. Recovery is just as mentally exhausting as it is physically.

That said, after years of health challenges, injuries, surgery, and doubt, I finally feel like I’m getting back to ME again! I’ve had so much amazing support from UCLA and family and i’ve learned so much! Today was my third day back high jumping since my ankle reconstruction over a year ago, and first day trying a full 8-step run, and I jumped my PR! The bar I haven’t been able to clear since the year I won state back in high school, and higher than I ever have in a practice!

I’ve tried a lot of things to feel good again mentally and physically, but what’s really helped me turn this corner is what I learned from my Grandpa this summer. He trained me with the philosophy that less is sometimes more, and held me to it. At first I argued, always wanting to push harder or faster because I thought that was what working hard meant. But he reminded me, “You don’t need to risk injury or health setbacks to prove you’re working hard. I promise by the end of the summer you will feel great! I’ll do the worrying.” 

I trusted him, and now I’m running workouts I never thought I could, and jumping my all time PR first attempt my first day back! And with no new injuries🥳 I’m in shock!! 
I’ve realized now that it’s not only possible but essential to learn the difference between working hard and breaking yourself. Strength isn’t just about pushing through, it’s also in the discipline to choose your health and long-term goals over short-term ego, impatience, or fear that could set you back further. A healthy confident athlete is a dangerous athlete. 

So excited to get back to UCLA, keep working hard, growing, and continuing this journey and awesome sport. The comeback is real 😋✨💪 
#ucla #uclatrackandfield #highjump

caption:
My Final Salute

My mom recognized early on that I was destined to be a performer because I was always dancing and entertaining friends and family whenever I could. To nurture this passion, she enrolled me in dance classes at Little Gym. However, I completely flubbed my first dance recital because all I wanted to do was sneak into the recreational gym across the hallway and swing on the bars. That experience made me realize I wanted to be a gymnast. 

As the years went by, I discovered that what I loved most about gymnastics wasn’t just the flips; it also provided me with a stage to perform. This realization ultimately deepened my love for dance. I see strong parallels between gymnastics and performing on stage, and that’s what this video represents.

@sujeyluna__, you are a gem! Thank you for helping me bring this vision to life. Thank you, @saraulias, aka my fav MUA, and to @suzimellano, @annaburnsy, @kairalyia, @sophialahmidi and @deannahong for capturing my @uclagymnastics journey so beautifully!

caption:
A few months ago, I was on an operating table getting my labrum repaired. Recovery has been one of the hardest things I’ve ever faced. It is filled with pain, sleepless nights, and moments where doubt felt louder than hope. But recovery isn’t linear. It’s messy and slow, yet also full of small victories like lifting my arm for the first time, getting cleared to lift weights, and finally stepping back into the pool.

Those wins remind me why I fight so hard for this sport. Being back in the water feels like coming home. This is not the end of recovery, but the beginning of a new chapter of my collegiate career. 💙

caption:
69.95 meters for 7th place at my first international competition!

Training has looked very different since I arrived in Hungary. After 8 practices with the @szombathelyi_dobo_se group, I am very pleased to produce 3 throws over 69.53.

I have gone from 60 throws a week to nearly 120 which is a really big accomplishment for me. With two more weeks of training here I can’t wait to continue building this connection as I look to get Hungarian citizenship.

A lot is changing in my throw with a different philosophy, notably throwing with 3 fingers instead of 4, which has been a learning curve.

I have much to learn and am cherishing every moment of this experience, I can’t wait to come back in the coming months.

caption:
Today I said goodbye to my last brother for college and I will not lie I cried. From day one we’ve always been blessed with an undying support for one another and today we’ve arrived at today where all 3 of us are in college. As African American men it is TRULY a blessing to be in this position. However, not only are we all in college but we are all collegiate athletes. 

My older brother Legend now attends Morehouse College and I know that the Lord put him in the best place after all of the  challenges he’s faced

My younger brother Kingston just moved into Arizona State today and will be competing in track and field. Yes, we do run the same event and, YES by the grace of the Lord, we will get to run against one another. 

We couldn’t have done it without our parents, so thank you Momma and Pops. I love you and I love my family 

Waring Fam On TOP! 💜

caption:
#1 – Not Communicating is Selfish

Basketball moves way too fast to stay quiet. When you don’t talk, you leave your teammates hanging—and that’s how trust gets broken. Even if you call out the wrong thing, your voice helps others react. Communication isn’t optional. It’s a skill that separates average from elite. And it costs nothing.

#2 – Your Sleep Schedule is Hurting You

You might get away with it as a freshman or sophomore… but it catches up. By senior year? You’re dragging. Poor sleep = slower recovery, mental fog, and more injuries. Want to stay on the court longer and play better? Start with your sleep. It’s the best recovery tool you’ve got.

#3 – The Grass Isn’t Always Greener

Yeah, NIL has changed the game. And I’m all for players getting paid 💰—go secure the bag. But chasing money alone can cost you culture, good teammates, and your peace of mind. Make sure the fit is right. Long-term happiness > short-term cheque. 

These won’t sit right with everybody - and that’s kindve the point. 

Let me know your thoughts on these topics… 👇🏽

caption:
End of an Era. 

I walked into a gym at barely 3 years old with a love of being able to flip around and a dream of going to the Olympics. I am now officially walking out of the gym over 20 years later, with a whole new love for this sport when I didn’t think it was possible. 

I’m going to be honest, my gymnastics journey was not an easy one. This sport, injuries, and certain individuals broke me to pieces, and I never thought that this was all something I could recover from. But I was wrong. These experiences turned me into a stronger person, a leader, and gave me a new perspective on what really matters.

Despite some of the hard times, there was a whole lot of great too. I literally got to flip for a living, travel all around the world and represent my country, compete at the Olympics & 3 World Championships, and most importantly, meet some of my best friends. I got to bring my version of art into the world of gymnastics. 

Specifically, this last year at UCLA is what truly helped me fall in love with the sport again. It was an incredibly special group, and it was the first time in a long time that I was able to freely do gymnastics with love again. 

Thank you to my parents, Denis, all my UCLA coaches, my teammates, and UCLA & Bruin Nation for the unwavering support throughout the years. I also wanted to shoutout all of my doctors, AT’s, and physios for all of their efforts to keep me together because that was not an easy task lol.

To young athletes - remember that everything happens for a reason, you are more than your sport, embrace your uniqueness, and that the good things you do will always come back to you. 

•

I was just a little kid in a pink velvet leotard with big dreams. All I did was for her.

Thank you gymnastics. 

P.S. You can still make it pretty far in gymnastics with a fear of flipping backwards :)

caption: Today the council members of the @cityofcommerce unanimously voted for a big change in our aquatics program. They decided that there will no longer be full time head swim coach, head women’s water polo coach and aquatics program director positions. This was made for the purpose of budget cuts, but what they will do to continue to “successfully” run the program is unmentioned and unclear to the community. Although I understand there are budgets that must be met throughout city activities, I do not support lessening these programs. Swimming and women’s water polo has been such a big foundation of what makes Commerce so special, lets hope these promises of a continued successful program don’t fall short through their changes as they have in the past. If you would wish to be better informed on this topic you can reach out to me or watch the full council meeting on their Facebook. https://fb.watch/BbH3snOARR/?mibextid=wwXIfr

caption:
@ucla was probably the worst 4 years of my life, but also the best? 

if you were to tell my 18-year-old self that i would put together more bone injuries than races (including 5 stress fractures in the span of a single year), and accomplished zero of my running-related goals, i probably would’ve felt like a failure.

but if i could do it all over again, i wouldn’t change a thing. if i had one less nap in a mri machine, one less delusional minute on a stationary bike or if my sesamoid wasn’t permanently in pieces - i probably wouldn’t have picked up a camera, learned graphic editing or realized i wanted to go back to writing.

i have a lot more to say about it and a lot more people to thank than than the character limits of an instagram caption, but for now a huge shoutout to @uclatrackandfield @uclaxc for seeing something in me and giving me space to make an impact on a team and in a sport i cared so much about, independent of performance, and for the opportunity to travel to more meets, make more connections and gain more experiences than i probably would have if i was actually healthy. 

TLDR; running wasn’t fulfilling me so i found something else that did that and change, and graduating from the #1 public university with honors in a competitive major, two minors, and all As was pretty cool too.

i’ll be taking the next step in this whole media thing by getting a MAMC and working as a creative video student intern for @floridagators, so i’ll have to report back if the west coast is still the best coast. my dumps are either portfolio-esque or the exact opposite, so here’s a chaotic carousel to bless your feed 😄🎓🐊

all grad photos shot by the talented @hritaco07 who was by my side the first day i did pick up a camera

p.s. i never actually put on my cap and gown, i was covering a track meet

caption:
Still Not Over The ESPYs 🏆

To think,  I once joked about “one day going to the ESPYS”… and then—that day turned out to be July 16th 2025.

Out of the blue, I got a call from Ryan, a producer for the ESPYS, inviting me to be a trophy presenter.

What followed was nothing short of surreal—from the legends I met to the incredible staff who brought this moment to life. A day I’ll remember forever.

This wasn’t just about walking a stage or holding a trophy.

It was about standing in the presence of greatness… and realizing God made it all possible.

Forever thankful.

Special thanks to Valdez, Ron Paul, Ryan, Amanda, Christie, and Jeanie—for trusting me with this amazing opportunity.

@samuel_scott.77, it was an honor sharing the stage with you… best 2025 Trophy Modeling Team Ever! 🙌🏽

Thanks to everyone behind the scenes—it was truly a blessing to work with you all.

“One of the most enduring aspects of Patrick’s legacy is his mantra: “We can do hard things.” These words became a rallying cry for those who knew him, especially during his courageous battle with NUT carcinoma. caption:
Today on the show is Aydon Stefanopoulos!

Aydon is a graduated senior out of Los Gatos High School in California. He will be a rising freshman this fall at UCLA. 

Aydon holds PRs of 1:51 for 800m, 4:06 for 1600m, 8:57 for 3200m, and 14:52 for 5K XC. He is the 2023 CIF D2 XC State Champion and a 2023 NXN qualifier.

Aydon and I had one of the most unpolished, raw, candid conversations I have ever had on The Sunday Shakeout. This was not an episode filled with positivity and glorified realities of the mental and physical side of our sport. We dive into the nitty gritty side of the sport of running. It's real, down to earth-dialogue.

As a junior, Aydon became a state champ and ran at NXN. This set a high bar to live up to his senior year. Unfortunately, however, Aydon has struggled with injuries and underperforming this past year. He failed to repeat at State XC, as well as qualify for NXN. He also did not have the redemption that he wanted this track season, despite setting PRs across multiple distances.

Aydon, in this episode, openly admits his struggles with confidence, self-doubt, and the mental toll of injuries and underperformance. Rather than just focusing on the accomplishments, he highlights the mistakes, regrets, and the emotional fallout of failure. He talks about being "not proud" of parts of his senior year, showing maturity and humility. 

Now, you might be asking:
"Why would I listen to such a melancholy podcast episode?"

Because despite setbacks, disappointments and the raw realities presented in my conversation with Aydon, he had a couple of mindset shifts: 

1. Moving from chasing perfection to valuing long-term health and enjoyment of the sport. Through setbacks and injuries, Aydon shares interesting insights on the importance of under training. Sounds crazy. But worth a listen.

2. Aydon's excitement about the next chapter at UCLA stems from a desire to learn, adapt, and improve, rather than prove anything. His ability to embrace uncertainty is instructive for all of us in the pursuit of excellence in our running careers.

I hope you enjoy this episode of The Sunday Shakeout!

caption:
The best is always saved for last!

I am elated to announce that this past Saturday, June 14th 2025, I have graduated from The University of California, Los Angeles with a Bachelor of Arts in Sociology on the Pre-Law track! To be a graduate from the number one public university as an African American man is extraordinary. 

To God, where would I be without your undeniable presence? You have allowed me to embark a journey that I have spoken about since I was eight years old. Whether I feel ontop of the world or life begins to become trying, Lord, my faith has not trembled. I trusted God when I completed my underclassmen years at the University of California, Berkeley, when I transferred to the University of Southern California, at UCLA, and thereafter. God showed me that my, seemingly, unaligned path is straight because my path is individualized. My God-given determination is the sole reason behind managing three of the top universities in the world and STILL completing my degree in four years. 

To myself, it has been one hell-of a ride. Thank you for staying the course even when you could not see the ending. It is because of your drive, poise, and discipline that you are where you are; do not let that go. Continue to be unapologetically you, making a name for yourself in a universe full of opportunity. You come from humble beginnings; you know what it is like to be without, which is why “no” has never been an option for you. From the streets of Oakland to the Hills of Beverly, your name rings bells. Taking a leap of faith and moving to Los Angeles was the best things you could have done for yourself; it ignighted your growth from a boy to a man. I’m proud of you!

This is only the beginning of what is next for me. I am grateful to live a life God has set for me.

Class Dismissed!

Di’Niko Bates 
B.A. Sociology 
Spring ’25
UCLA

🎥: @cancerblake

caption:
Yesterday, I graduated from UCLA.

College wasn’t just about lectures and exams — it was about becoming. These past four years taught me how to live on my own, think for myself, grow through discomfort, and open my heart to people from every walk of life. I arrived here as a stranger to this country, this culture, and this campus — and I leave with lifelong friendships, unforgettable lessons, and a version of myself I’m proud of.

I’ve laughed, failed, succeeded, healed, and changed — all on this campus. UCLA became my home, and the people I met here became my family.

To everyone who shared this journey with me — thank you.
To @ucla — thank you for shaping me.

Class of 2025 🎓💙

caption:
This cap, sash, and gown carries more than just a degree… they carry every sleepless night, every silent battle, every moment I wanted to give up but didn’t. I came to UCLA with a dream and walked this journey with more weight than most will ever know. As a student-athlete, I fought through the noise, through the doubts, the setbacks, and the struggles no one saw. Some believed in me. Some didn’t. But I kept going. And now, I graduate from the #1 public university in the nation. I made it. For the little girl who dreamed big, and for the woman who never gave up. The story isn’t over…it’s just beginning. Thank you to everyone who believed in me. Thank you to those pushed me to be better. Thank you to my coaches. Thank you to my parents. Thank you to my friends and loved ones. Thank you UCLA💙💛 

#graduated🎓 #graduate #ucla #studentathlete #ididit #girlonfire

Despite my whole profile being water polo related, I've (not so) secretly been a huge nerd the entire time. Today was my last day of undergrad, and I'll be graduating with a B.S. in Mathematics. All of these photos are just from today, a window into my last day of going to class, studying, writing reports, and leaving campus for the very last time. It's been such an amazing journey, and I'm so grateful for everything and everyone that has led me to this point.

Even though I'm leaving formal school, I hope to learn new things every day for the rest of my life. I am so excited for this next stage, and I can't wait to see what lies in store!!

With the Aquatics GB Diving Championships happening this week and weekend, some of you may be thinking why my name isn't on the list of competitors. 

After narrowly missing out on making the Paris 2024 Olympic Team, my relationship with diving has been put to the test. This year has been the first time in my career where I have decided to not compete at a national competition. The year has been about focusing on other goals and rebuilding my excitement and passion for the sport. It has also made me have a real think about my future in the sport and has definitely planted a seed to look at the possibility of LA 2028. 

I may not have been around this year, but best be sure I have hopes to be back competing internationally again next year.

caption:
I have no words… This was a very special win for me. I had the hardest time finding my throw despite a few amazing weeks of training, and was so thankful to pull something together in round 6. 

I felt somewhat defeated about half way into this competition, but am so proud of what I was able to achieve today. This was one of my big goals this season, to come in 3rd at this competition. 

The clap was a last ditch effort to find feeling in my throw and I feel nothing but blessed to sloppily put together a 70 meter throw that moved me from 4th to 3rd.

This is not how I planned to get it done, but everything happens for a reason. I am forever grateful for this learning experience, supportive team, and my coaches.

No matter what, keep pushing, trust your training, and have faith in everything you work so hard to accomplish.

First ever Big Ten medal for UCLA Track and Field! Go Bruins!

#bigten #podium #ncaa #hammerthrow #athlete #studentathlete

caption:
As this incredible chapter comes to a close, I find myself reflecting on the journey that I took on myself 4 years ago. Coming to UCLA from Israel was one of the biggest leaps I’ve ever taken — a leap into the unknown, into a new culture, and into a program with a legacy far greater than myself. And what I found here was more than I could have ever imagined.

Wearing those four letters across my chest wasn’t just about playing volleyball. It was about brotherhood, resilience, and chasing greatness alongside some of the most dedicated teammates and coaches I’ve ever known. Together, we climbed the mountain — not once, but twice — bringing home back-to-back national championships. Those moments, the roar of Pauley, the battles fought on the court, the silent early mornings, the grueling practices, the locker room laughs — they will stay with me for the rest of my life.

To my teammates: thank you for pushing me, believing in me, and becoming family.
To my coaches and staff: thank you for challenging me to grow as a player and as a man.
To the UCLA community and fans: thank you for embracing me, supporting me, and making a foreign country feel like home.

I leave with memories that have shaped who I am and friendships that will last a lifetime. UCLA Volleyball has given me everything — and now, it’s time to give my thanks, close this chapter, and carry its lessons with me into whatever comes next.

Once a Bruin, always a Bruin. 💙💛

With love,
Ido

Originally from New Jersey, Tre will join the @ocnoreasters for the upcoming 2025 USL2 season.

caption:
⭐️SENIOR SPOTLIGHT: COOPER ROBINSON⭐️

The final player we’d like to recognize for Senior Week is the iconic Cooper Robinson. Cooper’s presence on the court as a player and a leader has been so important to our program’s development, and we couldn’t be prouder to call him a Bruin. Robinson has collected many accolades, including (but certainly not limited to) a 2024 AVCA All-American pick, 2025 AVCA Player of the Week, being selected as the 2025 MPSF Offensive Player of the Week twice, and a two-time National Champion. During his four years with the team, he has collected over 117 blocks, 554 kills, and scored 688 points. Robinson’s leadership on and off the court has demonstrated his dedication to his teammates and to the sport as whole. Coop, thank you for everything, and we’re so excited for what your future holds!

#GoBruins

athlete.bio: A relentless competitor from a small town, this throws specialist combines raw power with impeccable technique. Known for his unwavering determination and infectious enthusiasm, he constantly pushes boundaries in pursuit of greatness.

caption:
4/11/15 ⏩ 4/11/25

This was an amazing weekend getting to throw with my youngest brother @jake.stafff in the same Continental Tour competition (and his first, at 19 years old!), and it was also a blast having our parents come out to support us and visit Oklahoma! 

This weekend is additionally significant to me because 10 years ago to this Sunday, 4/12/15, I broke my back in a weightlifting accident the day after throwing PRs in the discus and hammer at the JuCo Mt. Sac Relays (second picture, 4/11/15) and was told by many doctors I would never compete again. Grateful to God I made a full recovery, for feeling healthy and strong 10 years later, and as always for the journey. 

It always amazes me seeing that picture now that Jake, @jill_staff and I all went to and competed for the same university, and this weekend made it even cooler. Grateful and excited for what’s to come! 

#walkbyfaithnotbysight #StaffThrows

caption:
Meet @laurennn._.brownnn : A rower at @uclarowing , Lauren’s journey began with a dream of becoming a Division I athlete. She picked up rowing the summer before her junior year and quickly made her mark.

Her career highlights include placing third at @hocr1965 2022 in her high school’s first-ever women’s 4+ entry, helping her Varsity 8+ podium at Youth Nationals 2023, and competing in the @rowingincolor all-Black women’s 8+ at HOCR 2024—a moment that affirmed her place in the sport.

Lauren is passionate about diversity and representation in rowing, using her story to inspire and uplift other Black athletes. She believes in BRAID’s mission and works to ensure that young Black women know they belong in this space.

Lauren approaches every challenge with resilience, guided by her favorite mantra: “Trust the process.”

We celebrate Lauren for her leadership, strength, and dedication to shaping a more inclusive future in rowing! 🤩👏🏾

caption: This was the first day I met Alex. He finished 9th and I finished 8th in this race. We had no idea who each other were before the race, and barely did after. What we both had no idea about was the ten minutes we had spent running together as 14 year olds was only a fraction compared to the hundreds of hours we would spend running together in the 5 years that followed.  Two days later we met each other for the second time at the cba makeup test. While I wasn’t sure if I was going to end up attending cba, I knew that if I did, at least I had someone I could sit with at lunch. That thought ended up being true, and so much more. Alex was my first friend in high school and made me feel comfortable in a time when everything was new to me. When looking back that is what I think he was best at. Though he was academically gifted, I think his best attribute was his likableness. Someone that when they were absent, you would know straight away. Even though I met Alex through running, my best memories come from us just being bored with each other. Memories that if I described them they probably wouldn’t sound like much. But I think that’s when you know that you love someone. When you can do absolutely nothing with them and still cherish that time. Alex was my best friend, and he leaves a spot in my life that will never be filled.  Rest easy kemp ❤️

caption:
I’m leaving Louisville with a small hole in my heart. Mourning the losses, and the idea that I no longer get to roam these streets I’ve learned to call home. 

However, nothing will compare to the void in my soul upon arrival. 2020 was a devastating year to say the least. They say control what you can control, and I couldn’t control a global pandemic. Nor how the world reacts when an innocent Black woman is shot dead in her home. 

Hurt, lost, and confused as to how life can change so quickly. I had no choice but to deal with it and see it through. 870 miles later, my life was forever changed. 

Here’s to all the lovely memories in between. 

3 final fours
3 conference championships
2 national runner ups 

A trip to Brazil, Belize, Houston and Washington DC doing things I’ve never knew I wanted to do. Opening doors to rooms I didn’t know existed. And shaping me into the woman those in my corner knew I was capable of being. 

This program is built on grit, selflessness, unity, and the pursuit of happiness. I hope that I was able to leave this place with even a small fraction of all it has poured into me. Truly, and honestly the best place in the 🌍 

To the hottest coaching trio in college volleyball, thank you for seeing the vision. 

To all of my teammates, thank you for being there and making this experience so enjoyable.

To the 502, this really is the come up! Continue to show up and show out for one another. 

Thank you, Louisville. For everything. You will be missed dearly. 
L1C4 ❤️

Dear Seton Volleyball, where do I even begin. These past 4 years have brought me some of the best moments of my life. I can’t thank those around me enough. Thank you to my parents, coaches, teammates, friends and seton community for everything that you’ve blessed me with. The never ending support they have granted me with will never be forgotten. 

To my parents, thank you for all the time you spent driving to these games never missing one single set. Supporting me and my dreams. You guys have been there with me from the beginning. 

To my teammates, I couldn’t have asked for a better group of girls to spend my senior season with. You all made everyday worth showing up. I will miss playing monarch with you all, having to stop practice because of the laughter, the locker room before matches, and everything else. Y’all have helped me grow so much on and off the court and I can’t thank y’all enough. I am forever grateful to call you my friends and teammates. 

Thank you seton volleyball for forming me into the player I am today. Freshman me would’ve never thought of being district player of the year, 2 time first team all Ohio, 2 time first team league, 2 time first team district, a state champion and more. You gave me my best friends and the best memories I could’ve ever asked for. I am so grateful to be apart of history at seton. Being a state champion still doesn’t feel real and this is something I’ll never forget. #10out

caption:
I thought I would never idolize anyone in my life until I met @gabiguimaraes10 ♥️
 
Gabi, you are a confident, dedicated, genuine, and smart person who has absolutely set up the greatest role model for younger volleyball athletes like me.
 
You are impacting me not only because you are a world-elite-level volleyball player who is so athletic and skilled, but more importantly because of your positive personality as a human being. 
 
The cohesion that you, as a captain, brought to your team, the respect you gave to your opponents, referees, and fans, and also the care you showed about the injustices in society. You are always there to make people around you better.
 
Gabi, I think all of the good words can be applied to you. I am proud to tell everyone that you are my inspiration and motivation. I am so thankful for everything you have accomplished. Your impact on me is always beyond what happens on the court. Seeing you in Macau and interacting with you means so much to me that you don’t even know.
 
Please, please keep being the most authentic version of yourself! I will work super hard, and there’ll be one day when you’ll know me as a Chinese volleyball player!!!
 
Gabriela Guimarães, Te amo! ♥️🏐️🔥

caption:
November is National Adoption Awareness Month and I want to share my story of adoption as a way to encourage loving adults to provide forever families to kids in foster care.

I was adopted from Russia as a toddler through Nightlight Christian Adoptions. Had I stayed in an orphanage, my path in life would have been very similar to American kids and teens stuck in the foster care system who do not find a permanent home. I am thankful to have two brothers, adopted from Russia as well.

I had some medical issues when I was first adopted that put me in the hospital twice for a total of 14 days. The start of my life was rocky, but my adoptive parents changed the course of my life forever. Being adopted has given me a unique lens on life and I am grateful for my family, health and educational opportunities, especially knowing where I started out in life. 

Follow along with me this month to learn more about adoption and how you can change a child’s life.

caption:
September 8th: Peninsula South Bay Invitational @ Lakewood CC

2 days before the Peninsula Tourney, I broke my driver, so I had to play with a heavier and stiffer shaft. On the day of the tournament, I shot 64 (-10) to break a couple of records and won the individual title! 🔥

- broke the Lakewood CC course record by 2 strokes 
- broke the school record by 1 stroke
- broke my personal best by 3 strokes

I would like to say thank you to @pvphsgirlsgolf and @golflakewood for hosting this wonderful tournament! I am also thankful to be a part of the @apachegolf team as well! Without you guys, this event wouldn't have been possible. Shout-out to the greenskeeper for keeping the course conditions nice and slick!

https://www.pasadenastarnews.com/2023/09/12/san-gabriel-valley-girls-athlete-of-the-week-zoe-sprecher-arcadia/

Bonus vid of me teeing off in a sandstorm at the TTC @ Mission Hills Arnold Palmer after Lakewood. It was a good experience playing in 110 degree heat and sandstorm on 2nd day. 🏜️ Even though it was a hot and windy tournament, happy to push through and shot -1 71 on the last day to end up with even par for the tournament.

caption:
Did someone say EUROPEAN CHAMPION? 

This past year has been a very difficult one with many challenges to overcome. At the start of this season I didn’t think I would be diving, I couldn’t perform essential tasks like walking and bending down without experiencing excruciating pain in my right ankle day to day. So to think I could dive at an elite level again seemed very far out of my reach. 

I am so grateful for being able to have the opportunity to firstly be selected for this team and secondly be able to represent Great Britain and be a part of Team GB once again. 

A big Thank You goes out to everyone who has been a part of this journey with me because I don’t think I would be up on 10m or on this podium if it weren’t for your love and support. 

Jen (@coachleeming) Thank You for looking after me this past week and giving me back my confidence. I loved every second that I was Team Jen 🤍

And finally Tom (@ucla_diving) Thank You for believing in me when I didn’t believe in myself, you are amazing 💙💛
